correctness.rationale: Direct incidence proof and exhaustive check classify the forty four-vertex missing tetrahedra. Chain ranks (15,65,64,16) checked over F2, F3 and F101 and bounded over Q using chain identities. A fully indexed 95x95 integer submatrix of 64 degree-3 boundaries and 31 tetrahedral-sphere cycles has determinant -1 from 95 explicit unimodular pivots. This proves an integral H2 basis without torsion, and the transitive affine action yields primitivity for all forty. The standalone verifier uses the actual attached certificate and standard-library Python; no infinite theorem follows merely from the finite check.

value.rationale: The five-regular Clebsch graph is a classical sharp four-chromatic folded hypercube whose 31-dimensional second homology was known abstractly. The exact forty minimum-support geometric spheres, their primitivity and transitive symmetry, and a 31-element integral sphere basis provide independently useful cycle-level information absent from Betti numbers or rational characters. The nine-relation signed permutation presentation is canonical; no larger theorem or arbitrary parameter slice is required for this complete natural finite classification.
